kwargs.curator_enabled: optional; omit. When omitted the module reads `curator.enabled` itself from <profile>/config.yaml (bounded safe_read_regular_file, no credential file opened; Hermes default True when absent; None/'could_not_verify' for loader-ambiguous values, env interpolation, an active managed overlay, or an unreadable config). Pass a bool only to override; the section then says curator_enabled_source='caller'.
kwargs.clock: omit (tests only; monotonic seconds used for the 20 s cooperative budget and run_metrics.elapsed_ms)

consequences.skill_ledger.bookkeeping_orphans: Skills are recorded as active in skills/.usage.json with no skill folder of that name on disk; usage records are keyed by frontmatter name, so a skill whose folder is named differently is also counted.
consequences.skill_ledger.changes_by_recorded_actor: Recorded skill changes are counted by the actor label the ledger stores: curator (curator runs and background review forks), agent (tool calls in a conversation, which may include edits a person asked for or approved) and user (hermes curator archive, restore and purge commands); the ledger does not record who requested or reviewed a change, and edits made to skill files outside Hermes are not recorded at all.
consequences.skill_ledger.could_not_verify: The skill change ledger or bookkeeping metadata is absent, unreadable, malformed, or truncated by collection bounds; an absent ledger is not evidence that no skill changes occurred.
consequences.skill_ledger.noop_changes: The ledger contains change records whose recorded after-state is identical to the before-state (same file hashes, or no file recorded on either side); this shows the record, not why the change was made.
consequences.skill_ledger.orphan_backups: More than 20 MiB of backup blobs under .curator_backups/blobs are not referenced by any entry in the skill change ledger, or cannot be matched because there is no ledger; this measures disk use, not whether the files are still wanted.
consequences.skill_ledger.patch_storm: At least one skill has 10 or more ledger changes within a 24-hour window of ledger timestamps; the ledger records the changes, not why they were made or who asked for them.
consequences.skill_ledger.skill_growth: One or more skills grew to at least twice their initial recorded size and at least 8,000 bytes; blob sizes measure growth on disk but do not distinguish distilled reference depth from incident accumulation.
consequences.skill_ledger.version_churn: One or more skills accumulated at least 20 distinct SKILL.md content versions in the ledger; this counts recorded hashes, not the size or nature of each change.

free_strings.what: absolute real path of the skill folder <profile>/skills/<name> or <profile>/skills/<category>/<name> for a ledger skill whose folder exists now; null when it is not located (then counted in skills_without_folder_count)
free_strings.why_safe: an existing folder inside the audited skills tree, at most two levels below skills/, never a symlink or credential-named entry; located by the ledger's recorded SKILL.md location (part after a /skills/ segment) or, when the ledger records none, by a unique folder name in a complete non-following walk; the raw ledger name is never emitted. EvidenceSerializer.scalar keeps it unchanged (absolute path that resolves and lstat's to itself) provided it still exists at serialisation time.

free_strings.what: the located entries among the 10 skills with the most ledger changes (subset of skills[].path); the rest of the 10 are counted in top_skills_by_changes.unlocated_count
the located entries among the 10 skills with the largest verified growth ratio (subset of skills[].path); the rest counted in top_skills_by_growth.unlocated_count

notes: Envelope: make_component_envelope -> {ok, status (legacy pass/fail), error, coverage, classification, findings, skill_ledger, run_metrics}. adapt_component_result drops ok/status/error/classification (recomputed), keeps coverage, and copies every other top-level key, so `skill_ledger` AND `run_metrics` survive into the adapted result. The caller must store `run_metrics` outside the fingerprinted report (store.finalize_run only copies named measurement sections, so it is ignored unless added there).
Section status is completed|not_measured; envelope status is the legacy pass/fail from make_component_envelope; coverage is verified|could_not_verify.

Every consequence is one fixed sentence per rule (CONSEQUENCES); add each to FINDING_CONSEQUENCES so ALLOWED_FINDING_CONSEQUENCES (and thus audit.evidence.CODE_LABELS / VOCABULARY) contains it; rule ids must join RULE_IDS (also feeds VOCABULARY).

Finding evidence holds only numbers/booleans and the vocabulary labels reason/truncated_by: name lists were removed from finding evidence because finding_dto drops lists; the names are in the section. truncated_by is only present when not null (finding_dto drops None).

Dates are numbers: date_range.earliest_epoch_s/latest_epoch_s (ints from ledger timestamps) and changes_by_month[].year/month (ints); nothing depends on the wall clock. run_metrics.elapsed_ms is the only run-dependent value. Time-budget truncation (truncated_by time_budget) can still differ between runs on a very slow machine; that is coverage, not a measurement.

Free strings: the section and findings emit no string that EvidenceSerializer would tokenise. Skill names are never emitted: a ledger skill is reported by the absolute real path of its existing folder (skills[].path, top_skills_by_*.paths), else null / counted (skills_without_folder_count, top_skills_by_*.unlocated_count). Not located = folder absent (deleted or renamed), recorded location not on disk, several folders of that name, deeper than skills/<category>/<name>, a refused symlink or credential-named entry at that place, an incomplete skills walk (time budget, entry cap, unreadable tree), or a ledger name that is not one plain path component (e.g. shaped like an absolute path). Usage-record and bundled-manifest names have no folder by definition: bookkeeping_orphans holds counts only. Tests prove: sealed section == raw section, no dict with an hmac field, two runs sealed with fresh serializer keys are identical, canary names (incl. an absolute path to an existing file outside skills/) never appear. A kept path must still exist when the report is serialised; if it vanished in between, the serializer would turn it into an unresolved_reference token.
